title_as_printed: The past, present, and future of sleep measurement in mild cognitive impairment and early dementia - towards a core outcome set: a scoping review

Task_Type.quote: This scoping review determines how sleep is currently measured and reported in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and early dementia

Category.reason: Questionnaires, the dominant measurement (131 studies), are C5, which the registry carries. Polysomnography/EEG (C2, 88 studies) and actigraphy (C4 sensors, 38 studies) are secondary domains the registry omits.
Category.quote: sleep was measured most commonly by validated questionnaires (n = 12 586, N = 131). Fewer participants underwent polysomnography (PSG) (n = 3492, N = 88) and actigraphy (n = 3359, N = 38)

Validation_Type.quote: This review follows the PRISMA Guidelines for Scoping Reviews.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: The pooled count of unique participants in a review, which the definition allows for reviews. The paper also reports 188 included full texts (178 unique studies) and 18,770 non-unique participants.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: Sleep data was reported on 17 139 unique, diagnostically diverse participants (n).

Publication_Year.reason: Advance access 4 April 2022; SLEEP vol. 45 no. 7 (2022).

ADNI_Dependent.reason: A literature review; it uses no dataset.
ADNI_Dependent.quote: CINAHL, Embase, Medline, Psychinfo, and British Nursing Index databases were searched from inception—March 12, 2021.

notes: N = 17,139 is a scoping review's pooled participant count. The definition allows it, but litreview_stats.sample_n parses it as a participant N (it has no study-count unit), so this review enters the sample-size distribution alongside primary studies and pulls it upward.
